papers.title: High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Predominance and Genotypic Diversity among Women with Cervical Complaints in Bangladesh
papers.abstract: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the main cause of cervical cancer (CC) in Bangladesh. This study investigated HPV occurrence, circulating genotypes, and their phylogenetic relationships among Bangladeshi women with cervical complaints. It also characterized the complete genome, lineage, and mutations of an HPV45 strain from Bangladesh. Methods Cervical swabs from 102 women with cervical complaints were obtained at a tertiary-care hospital in Bangladesh. HPV was detected by PCR amplification using gene-specific primers. Among the HPV-positive samples, those showing strong PCR band intensity were selected for Sanger sequencing of the partial L1 gene. Complete genome sequencing of a representative HPV45 strain was sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq X Plus platform. Phylogenetic analyses were conducted using MAFFT, IQ-TREE2, and RAxML-NG. Mutational, structural, and protein stability analyses were performed using bioinformatic and structural modeling tools. Results HPV DNA was detected in 47.1% (48/102) of participants. Of the 36 samples selected for Sanger sequencing based on strong PCR band intensity, 21 were successfully sequenced. Genotyping of sequenced strains revealed a predominance of high-risk HPV genotypes (95.45%); HPV16 (68.18%) and HPV18 (13.63%). Phylogenetic analyses demonstrated genotype-specific clustering and close genetic relatedness to globally circulating strains. Complete genomic characterization of an HPV45 strain (HPV_MGH-TT01) revealed a 7,849-bp genome belonging to the A2 sublineage, with 98.0-99.9% nucleotide identity to global reference strains. Multiple amino acid substitutions were identified, particularly within the E2 protein, although structural analyses predicted only minor conformational alterations. Conclusions The predominance of high-risk HPV genotypes and the genomic characterization of HPV45 highlight the importance of large-scale genomic surveillance and expanded molecular screening for preventing CC in Bangladesh.
papers.journal: Journal of Infection and Public Health

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to investigate the occurrence and genotypic diversity of human papillomavirus (HPV) among Bangladeshi women with cervical complaints. HPV DNA was detected in 47.1% of participants, with high-risk genotypes predominating, particularly HPV16 and HPV18. The complete genome of an HPV45 strain was characterized, revealing a 7,849-bp genome belonging to the A2 sublineage with high nucleotide identity to global reference strains. The study highlights the importance of genomic surveillance and molecular screening for preventing cervical cancer in Bangladesh. However, the findings are based on a single tertiary-care hospital and a limited sample size, which may restrict generalisability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: HPV 是孟加拉国 宫颈癌 (CC) 的主要原因。本研究调查了患有宫颈疾病的孟加拉国女性中 HPV 的发生率、循环基因型及其系统发育关系。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 从孟加拉国一家三级医院采集了 102 名患有宫颈疾病的女性的宫颈拭子。该研究重点关注 HPV 阳性样本,并对来自孟加拉国的 HPV45 毒株的完整 基因组 进行了表征。
elements_zh.methods: 使用基因特异性引物通过 PCR 扩增检测 HPV。在HPV阳性样本中,选择PCR条带强度较强的样本进行部分L1基因的Sanger测序。在 Illumina NovaSeq X Plus 平台上对代表性 HPV45 毒株进行完整的 基因组 测序。
elements_zh.main_results: 47.1% (48/102) 的参与者检测到 HPV DNA。对测序菌株的基因分型显示,高危型HPV 基因型占主导地位(95.45%);HPV16(68.18%)和HPV18(13.63%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 高危型HPV 基因型的优势和 HPV45 的基因组特征凸显了大规模 基因组监测 和扩大分子筛查对于孟加拉国预防 CC 的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,孟加拉国需要开展有针对性的 HPV 筛查和 监测 计划,以更好地了解和管理 HPV 相关的 监测。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于一家三级医院且样本量相对较小,这可能会影响普适性。由于研究的设计和范围,证据是中等的。

papers.title_zh: 孟加拉国宫颈疾病女性的高风险 人乳头瘤病毒 优势和基因型多样性
papers.source_body_en: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the main cause of cervical cancer (CC) in Bangladesh. This study investigated HPV occurrence, circulating genotypes, and their phylogenetic relationships among Bangladeshi women with cervical complaints. It also characterized the complete genome, lineage, and mutations of an HPV45 strain from Bangladesh. Methods Cervical swabs from 102 women with cervical complaints were obtained at a tertiary-care hospital in Bangladesh. HPV was detected by PCR amplification using gene-specific primers. Among the HPV-positive samples, those showing strong PCR band intensity were selected for Sanger sequencing of the partial L1 gene. Complete genome sequencing of a representative HPV45 strain was sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq X Plus platform. Phylogenetic analyses were conducted using MAFFT, IQ-TREE2, and RAxML-NG. Mutational, structural, and protein stability analyses were performed using bioinformatic and structural modeling tools. Results HPV DNA was detected in 47.1% (48/102) of participants. Of the 36 samples selected for Sanger sequencing based on strong PCR band intensity, 21 were successfully sequenced. Genotyping of sequenced strains revealed a predominance of high-risk HPV genotypes (95.45%); HPV16 (68.18%) and HPV18 (13.63%). Phylogenetic analyses demonstrated genotype-specific clustering and close genetic relatedness to globally circulating strains. Complete genomic characterization of an HPV45 strain (HPV_MGH-TT01) revealed a 7,849-bp genome belonging to the A2 sublineage, with 98.0-99.9% nucleotide identity to global reference strains. Multiple amino acid substitutions were identified, particularly within the E2 protein, although structural analyses predicted only minor conformational alterations. Conclusions The predominance of high-risk HPV genotypes and the genomic characterization of HPV45 highlight the importance of large-scale genomic surveillance and expanded molecular screening for preventing CC in Bangladesh.

papers.title: Nonclinical pharmacology and toxicology studies of LY01620, a therapeutic mRNA vaccine against human papillomavirus 16-related cancers
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and related cancers remain significant public health concerns worldwide. Among high-risk HPV genotypes, HPV16 demonstrates the highest epidemiological prevalence. The viral oncoproteins E6 and E7 are crucial drivers of HPV16-associated carcinogenesis and have become key therapeutic targets for treating HPV16-related cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and cancers. HPV prophylactic vaccines have been widely implemented in clinical practice; however, effective therapeutic interventions for infected individuals remain limited. Therefore, the development of therapeutic HPV vaccines is urgently needed. LY01620 is an investigational mRNA therapeutic vaccine targeting HPV16 E6/E7 antigens. To support LY01620’s clinical trial application and development, comprehensive nonclinical studies were conducted, including immunogenicity evaluations in mice and rats, anti-tumor activity and mechanistic studies in C3.43 tumor-bearing mice, single-dose tissue distribution study in rats, and a GLP-compliant repeated-dose toxicity study in rats combined with toxicokinetics, local irritation, and immunotoxicity assessments. LY01620 demonstrated strong immunogenicity in mice and rats and exhibited significant anti-tumor activity through inducing a strong Th1-polarized immune response, increasing frequency of antigen-specific T cells, and enhancing infiltration of CD8 + T cells and mature macrophages into tumors. LY01620 mRNA exhibited sustained accumulation in inguinal lymph nodes and spleens, potentially facilitating persistent antigen presentation and prolonged immunological effects. In the repeated-dose toxicity study in SD rats, LY01620 exhibited a favorable safety profile, with the no observed adverse effect level was the highest dose of 300 μg/animal. In conclusion, preclinical studies have demonstrated that LY01620 exhibited favorable mechanism of action-related efficacy and a well-tolerated safety profile, supporting its further development.

papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染和相关癌症仍然是全球重大的公共卫生问题。在高危型HPV基因型中,HPV16表现出最高的流行病学患病率。病毒癌蛋白E6和E7是HPV16相关癌变的关键驱动因素,并已成为治疗HPV16相关宫颈上皮内瘤变和癌症的关键治疗靶点。HPV预防药疫苗已广泛应用于临床;然而,针对感染者的有效治疗干预措施仍然有限。因此,迫切需要开发治疗性HPV 疫苗。LY01620 是一种针对 HPV16 E6/E7 抗原的研究中 mRNA 治疗药物 疫苗。为支持LY01620的临床试验应用和开发,开展了全面的非临床研究,包括小鼠和大鼠的免疫原性评估、C3.43荷瘤小鼠的抗肿瘤活性和机制研究、大鼠单剂量组织分布研究、以及结合毒代动力学、局部刺激和免疫毒性评估的符合GLP标准的大鼠重复剂量毒性研究。LY01620在小鼠和大鼠中表现出很强的免疫原性,并通过诱导强Th1极化免疫应答、增加抗原特异性T细胞的频率、增强CD8+T细胞和成熟巨噬细胞向肿瘤的浸润而表现出显着的抗肿瘤活性。LY01620 mRNA 在腹股沟淋巴结和脾脏中表现出持续积累,可能促进持续的抗原呈递和延长免疫效应。在SD大鼠重复给药毒性研究中,LY01620表现出良好的安全性,最高剂量为300μg/只,未观察到不良反应。总之,临床前研究表明LY01620表现出良好的作用相关功效机制和良好的耐受性安全性,支持其进一步开发。

papers.title: Human papillomavirus genotype distribution and concordance between vaginal and prior lower genital tract neoplasia: a tissue-based study
papers.abstract: Women previously treated for HPV-associated lower genital tract neoplasia remain at increased risk of developing vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VaIN). However, data on HPV genotype concordance based on direct tissue analysis remain limited. We evaluated HPV genotype distribution and concordance between HPV-associated VaIN2+ (VaIN2, VaIN3, or invasive vaginal carcinoma) and previous HPV-associated lower genital tract neoplasia using lesion-specific HPV genotyping of archived tissue specimens. This retrospective single-center cohort study included women with histologically confirmed and HPV-associated VaIN2+​. HPV genotyping was performed on formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue using a multiplex real-time PCR assay. HPV genotype distributions were compared between women with and without previous HPV-associated lower genital tract neoplasia. Genotype concordance between paired lesions and factors associated with VaIN3+ were also evaluated. Of 72 eligible women, 39 (54.2%) had previous lower genital tract neoplasia. The vaginal lesion was genotyped in 56 women (30 with, 26 without previous neoplasia); both lesions were evaluable and HPV-positive in 28. HPV16 predominated, detected in 51.8% of the lesions with a valid result. HPV16 and/or HPV18 positivity was more frequent in women with previous neoplasia (66.7% vs. 38.5%; p = 0.059), as was VaIN3+ (66.7% vs. 42.3%; p = 0.106); neither remained below 0.05 after adjustment for multiplicity. HPV16 was independently associated with VaIN3+ (adjusted OR 3.84, 95%CI: 1.22–12.93; p = 0.024). Among the 28 paired cases, concordance was complete in 23 (82.1%), partial in four (14.3%) and absent in one (3.6%); 27 (96.4%) shared at least one genotype. The interval between lesions reached 31.8 years. Direct tissue-based HPV genotyping showed a high frequency of shared HPV genotypes between VaIN2 + and previous HPV-associated LGT neoplasia. This is consistent with long-term persistence or reactivation of the same HPV genotype, although reinfection with the same genotype cannot be excluded and a common clonal origin was not assessed. Women with previous neoplasia more often had HPV16 and/or HPV18 positivity and VaIN3+, but these exploratory differences were imprecise. The findings support long-term surveillance after treatment of cervical high-grade lesions. Institution: University Hospital Královské Vinohrady, Prague, Czech Republic; reference number EK-VP/34/00/2025; approved 7 May 2025.

papers.title: HPV DNA integration is correlated with persistence or progression of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 2 (CIN2).
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE(S): To determine whether identical HPV-human DNA integrations in cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 (CIN2) lesions are retained during progression to squamous cervical carcinoma (SCC) and whether such integrations can predict lesion persistence or progression. METHODS: Longitudinal cervical samples were analyzed using multiplexed DNA hybridization-capture targeting 225 HPV types, followed by short-read sequencing to identify HPV-human DNA integration junctions. Integration events were evaluated in (i) serial samples from CIN lesions that progressed to SCC and (ii) a baseline cohort of 23 patients with incident CIN2. Clinical outcomes (regression vs persistence/progression) were compared by integration status using Fisher's Exact Test and multivariable Bayesian logistic regression to estimate effect sizes in the setting of small sample size. RESULTS: Identical HPV-human DNA integrations were preserved across serial samples in seven CIN lesions that progressed to SCC, supporting their biological relevance in carcinogenesis. In the CIN2 cohort, no integrations were detected in any of the 12 patients whose lesions regressed, whereas integrations were present in four of eleven patients whose lesions persisted or progressed (p=0.04). Bayesian logistic regression estimated a 22-fold higher odds of persistence/progression when integration was detected at baseline CIN2 diagnosis. HPV16 positivity was also associated with persistence/progression, with a smaller estimated effect size (9.4-fold higher odds), consistent with prior epidemiologic observations. CONCLUSION(S): HPV DNA integrations were associated with CIN2 persistence and progression, and identical integrations were retained during evolution to SCC. Integration analysis at CIN2 diagnosis may identify lesions at highest risk for progression, providing a biomarker to refine clinical management and reduce unnecessary excisional procedures.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在确定 CIN2 病变中的 HPV-人类 DNA 整合在进展为鳞状细胞癌期间是否保留,以及这种整合是否可以预测病变的持续或进展。这填补了了解 HPV DNA 整合在宫颈癌发生中的作用的知识空白。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用多重 DNA 杂交捕获和短读长测序分析了进展为 SCC 的 CIN2 病变的纵向宫颈样本以及 23 名发生 CIN2 患者的基线 队列研究。
elements_zh.methods: 使用多重 DNA 杂交捕获和短读长测序来分析样本的 HPV 类型,以识别 HPV-人类 DNA 整合连接点。使用费舍尔精确检验和多变量贝叶斯逻辑回归来比较临床结果。
elements_zh.main_results: 七个进展为鳞状细胞癌的 CIN2 病变中保留了相同的 HPV-人类 DNA 整合。在 CIN2 队列研究 中,11 名病变持续或进展的患者中有 4 名出现整合(p=0.04)。当在基线 CIN2 诊断 检测到整合时,贝叶斯逻辑回归估计持续/进展的几率高出 22 倍。HPV16 阳性也与持续/进展相关,估计效应较小(几率高 9.4 倍)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,HPV DNA 整合与 CIN2 持续存在和进展相关,并且在 进化 至 SCC 期间保留了相同的整合。这提供了一种生物标志物来识别进展风险最高的病变,从而可能减少不必要的切除手术。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: CIN2 诊断 的整合分析可以识别进展风险最高的病变,从而提供生物标志物来完善临床管理并减少不必要的切除手术。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到样本量小和贝叶斯逻辑回归的使用的限制,这可能会影响研究结果的普遍性。证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 目的:确定 2 级宫颈上皮内瘤变 (CIN2) 病变中相同的 HPV-人类 DNA 整合在进展为鳞状宫颈癌 (SCC) 的过程中是否保留,以及此类整合是否可以预测病变持续或进展。方法:使用针对 225 种 HPV 类型的多重 DNA 杂交捕获分析纵向宫颈样本,然后进行短读长测序以识别 HPV-人类 DNA 整合连接点。在 (i) 进展为 SCC 的 CIN 病变的连续样本和 (ii) 23 名发生 CIN2 的患者的基线 队列研究 中评估整合事件。使用 Fisher 精确检验和多变量贝叶斯逻辑回归通过积分状态比较临床结果(回归与持续/进展),以估计小样本量设置中的效应大小。结果:七个进展为鳞状细胞癌的 CIN 病变的系列样本中保留了相同的 HPV-人类 DNA 整合,支持了它们在致癌过程中的生物学相关性。在 CIN2 队列研究 中,12 名病变消退的患者中均未检测到整合,而 11 名病变持续或进展的患者中有 4 名存在整合(p=0.04)。当在基线 CIN2 诊断 检测到整合时,贝叶斯逻辑回归估计持续/进展的几率高出 22 倍。HPV16 阳性也与持续/进展相关,估计效应较小(几率高 9.4 倍),与之前的流行病学观察结果一致。结论:HPV DNA 整合与 CIN2 持续存在和进展相关,并且在 进化 至 SCC 期间保留了相同的整合。CIN2 诊断 的整合分析可以识别进展风险最高的病变,从而提供生物标志物来完善临床管理并减少不必要的切除手术。

papers.title: Assessing resource allocation and exploring measures to promote human papillomavirus vaccination in Beijing, China
papers.abstract: This study aimed to comprehensively assess the availability and resource allocation of HPV vaccination services in Beijing, and to identify effective strategies for improving public vaccine acceptance and uptake. An ecological study was conducted across 499 vaccination clinics in Beijing in 2024. A structured questionnaire was administered to collect data on HPV vaccination service provision at each vaccination clinic. Nearest neighbor analysis, kernel density analysis, hot-spot analysis, and the resource-utilization efficiency matrix were applied to assess the allocation and utilization of vaccination resources. A negative binomial regression model was employed to estimate the incidence rate ratio (IRR) for HPV vaccination. In Beijing, 39.28% of health-care facilities and 93.59% of vaccination clinics provided HPV vaccination services. Among these vaccination clinics, 79.87% were based in primary health-care facilities, while only 4.07% were adult vaccination clinics located in secondary or tertiary hospitals. Mean weekly service hours and staffing were lower in immunization clinics (8 hours, 10 staff) than in adult clinics (27 hours, 18 staff). Electronic queuing systems (IRR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.21–1.73), offline vaccination education (IRR = 1.43, 95% CI: 1.07–1.92), and ≥4 parental classes monthly (IRR = 2.93, 95% CI: 1.29–6.65) were significantly associated with higher HPV vaccination coverage. To alleviate shortages of HPV vaccination resources at routine immunization clinics and given the stronger service capacity of current adult vaccination clinics, pilot expansion at selected secondary and tertiary facilities may be warranted, pending formal cost-effectiveness evaluation. Initiatives such as conducting parental education and establishing electronic queuing systems were associated with higher vaccination doses.

papers.source_body_en: This study aimed to comprehensively assess the availability and resource allocation of HPV vaccination services in Beijing, and to identify effective strategies for improving public vaccine acceptance and uptake. An ecological study was conducted across 499 vaccination clinics in Beijing in 2024. A structured questionnaire was administered to collect data on HPV vaccination service provision at each vaccination clinic. Nearest neighbor analysis, kernel density analysis, hot-spot analysis, and the resource-utilization efficiency matrix were applied to assess the allocation and utilization of vaccination resources. A negative binomial regression model was employed to estimate the incidence rate ratio (IRR) for HPV vaccination. In Beijing, 39.28% of health-care facilities and 93.59% of vaccination clinics provided HPV vaccination services. Among these vaccination clinics, 79.87% were based in primary health-care facilities, while only 4.07% were adult vaccination clinics located in secondary or tertiary hospitals. Mean weekly service hours and staffing were lower in immunization clinics (8 hours, 10 staff) than in adult clinics (27 hours, 18 staff). Electronic queuing systems (IRR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.21–1.73), offline vaccination education (IRR = 1.43, 95% CI: 1.07–1.92), and ≥4 parental classes monthly (IRR = 2.93, 95% CI: 1.29–6.65) were significantly associated with higher HPV vaccination coverage. To alleviate shortages of HPV vaccination resources at routine immunization clinics and given the stronger service capacity of current adult vaccination clinics, pilot expansion at selected secondary and tertiary facilities may be warranted, pending formal cost-effectiveness evaluation. Initiatives such as conducting parental education and establishing electronic queuing systems were associated with higher vaccination doses.

papers.title: Undergraduate nursing students’ perceptions of human papillomavirus and its prevention: a qualitative study guided by the Health Belief Model
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a significant public health concern and the leading cause of cervical cancer as well as several other malignancies. Despite its importance, there is limited qualitative evidence examining nursing students’ perceptions of HPV and its prevention in Saudi Arabia. This study sought to investigate undergraduate nursing students’ perceptions of HPV and its prevention using the Health Belief Model (HBM) as a theoretical framework. This descriptive qualitative study utilized six focus group discussions (FGDs) involving 36 eligible undergraduate nursing students from the University of Bisha, Saudi Arabia. Participants were recruited through purposive sampling. Thematic analysis was conducted based on the HBM, employing its six constructs as predefined overarching analytic domains, while specific subthemes were developed inductively from participants’ accounts. The six deductive themes, perceived susceptibility, perceived severity, perceived benefits, perceived barriers, cues to action, and self-efficacy, correspond to the HBM constructs. Inductively developed subthemes included inadequate understanding of HPV, low perceived personal susceptibility, misconceptions about vaccination safety and transmission, stigma, and challenges in discussing sensitive sexual health issues. Participants also described perceived institutional and educational influences on communication preparedness, professional relevance, and HPV knowledge. These findings do not demonstrate the efficacy of specific teaching methods but highlight educational needs within this sample. Undergraduate nursing students identified knowledge gaps, misunderstandings, stigma, societal challenges, and a lack of confidence when discussing HPV prevention. The findings emphasize the necessity of providing evidence-based and culturally sensitive education on HPV transmission, screening, vaccination, reproductive health issues, stigma, and communication skills. These needs could be met through case-based learning, role-playing, simulation and communication training, but the present study did not evaluate their effectiveness and further research is needed.

papers.title: HPV-Associated oropharyngeal cancer: Changes in epidemiological profile and prognostic implications
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma has altered the epidemiology and prognostic interpretation of head and neck cancer. This narrative critical review examines changes in incidence and demographic distribution, the validity of HPV-related tumor classification, and the implications of viral status for survival and treatment decisions. Literature indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE through 2026 was examined alongside professional guidelines and institutional cancer-prevention resources. Population-based studies document a marked increase in HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer in several high-income settings, with an increasingly important burden among older men, while estimates remain heterogeneous across regions. HPV-positive tumors generally have more favorable survival than HPV-negative tumors, but smoking exposure, disease extent, and discordance between p16 and HPV-specific tests modify this advantage. Staging revisions acknowledge the distinct disease phenotype, including refinements introduced in 2026. Randomized trials demonstrate that favorable prognosis cannot justify indiscriminate treatment reduction, although selected postoperative de-intensification approaches are promising. Vaccination reduces vaccine-type oral HPV infection, whereas an effect on incident oropharyngeal cancer will require longer observation. Prognostic assessment should integrate viral attribution, anatomical stage, patient characteristics, treatment quality, and long-term functional outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the evolving epidemiological profile of HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer, emphasizing its impact on head and neck cancer demographics and prognosis. The evidence highlights the increasing incidence among older men in high-income regions and the heterogeneity of estimates globally. HPV-positive tumors show better survival outcomes, but factors like smoking, disease stage, and test discordance can alter this. Staging revisions reflect the distinct disease phenotype. papers.title: Beyond Normal Cytology: Clinical Significance of HPV 16/18 Positivity in a High-Risk Adolescent — A Case Report
papers.abstract: Background: High-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is a major etiological factor for cervical cancer. Appropriate risk-based management is essential, especially in young patients with normal cytology but positive HR-HPV test results. Case presentation: A 17-year old single female with a history of commercial sex work presented with recurrent vaginal discharge and previously treated genital warts. She reported having multiple sexual partners with inconsistent condom use after leaving sex work. Gynecological examination revealed a reddish cervix with whitish discharge, while Pap smear results were normal. However, HR HPV testing was positive. Colposcopic evaluation showed acetowhite changes at the 11–12 o’clock position with negative iodine uptake on Lugol’s test. A loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) biopsy was performed, and histopathological results were pending. Discussion: According to the 2019 ASCCP risk-based guidelines, patients with positive result of HR-HPV and normal cytology generally have a low immediate risk of CIN3+and may be managed with surveillance. However, the presence of high-risk HPV types, particularly HPV 16/18, justifies early colposcopic evaluation despite normal cytology. The Indonesian Gynecologic Oncology (Himpunan Onkologi Ginekologi Indonesia/HOGI) guidelines similarly recommend colposcopy or visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) in HRHPV-positive patients, followed by appropriate intervention if lesions are detected. Conclusions: This case highlights the importance of individualized, risk-based management in HR-HPV-positive patients. Early colposcopic assessment may be warranted even with normal cytology, particularly in high-risk populations, to ensure timely detection and treatment of precancerous lesions.

analysis.methods: The patient underwent gynecological examination, Pap smear, HR-HPV testing, and colposcopic evaluation. A loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) biopsy was performed, and histopathological results were pending.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Early colposcopic assessment may be warranted even with normal cytology, particularly in high-risk populations, to ensure timely detection and treatment of precancerous lesions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report on the statistical power or generalisability of the findings. The evidence is based on a single case report, which limits its strength to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This case report highlights the clinical significance of HR-HPV positivity in a high-risk adolescent with normal cytology. The patient, a 17-year-old female with a history of commercial sex work, presented with recurrent vaginal discharge and genital warts. HR-HPV testing was positive, while Pap smear results were normal. Colposcopic evaluation revealed acetowhite changes, prompting the need for further investigation. The authors emphasize the importance of individualized, risk-based management in HR-HPV-positive patients, particularly those with high-risk HPV types such as 16/18. They suggest that early colposcopic assessment may be necessary despite normal cytology to detect precancerous lesions. The study is limited to a single case report, which provides moderate evidence for the need for surveillance in such patients.

papers.title_zh: 超越正常细胞学:高危青少年 HPV 16/18 阳性的临床意义 — 病例报告
papers.source_body_en: Background: High-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) infection is a major etiological factor for cervical cancer. Appropriate risk-based management is essential, especially in young patients with normal cytology but positive HR-HPV test results. Case presentation: A 17-year old single female with a history of commercial sex work presented with recurrent vaginal discharge and previously treated genital warts. She reported having multiple sexual partners with inconsistent condom use after leaving sex work. Gynecological examination revealed a reddish cervix with whitish discharge, while Pap smear results were normal. However, HR HPV testing was positive. Colposcopic evaluation showed acetowhite changes at the 11–12 o’clock position with negative iodine uptake on Lugol’s test. A loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP) biopsy was performed, and histopathological results were pending. Discussion: According to the 2019 ASCCP risk-based guidelines, patients with positive result of HR-HPV and normal cytology generally have a low immediate risk of CIN3+and may be managed with surveillance. However, the presence of high-risk HPV types, particularly HPV 16/18, justifies early colposcopic evaluation despite normal cytology. The Indonesian Gynecologic Oncology (Himpunan Onkologi Ginekologi Indonesia/HOGI) guidelines similarly recommend colposcopy or visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) in HRHPV-positive patients, followed by appropriate intervention if lesions are detected. Conclusions: This case highlights the importance of individualized, risk-based management in HR-HPV-positive patients. Early colposcopic assessment may be warranted even with normal cytology, particularly in high-risk populations, to ensure timely detection and treatment of precancerous lesions.

papers.title: 1064 PapillomaVax: a compact 9-mer universal polyepitope mRNA vaccine spanning HPV16 E2, E5, E6, and E7 drives simultaneous multi-specific CD8 + T cell priming in primary human PBMCs
papers.abstract: Background Therapeutic HPV vaccination requires broad, multi-specific CD8 + CTL responses against constitutively expressed viral oncoproteins to sustain tumor control and limit immune escape through selective antigen downregulation, documented in immune-edited HPV-positive tumors. The 27-mer flanking sequence format is commonly used but its coding burden constrains multi-protein coverage. We systematically quantified the immunological cost of a compact 9-mer format and applied the resulting design principles to a 16-epitope HPV16-specific polyepitope mRNA encoding known immunogenic epitopes from E2, E5, E6, and E7 proteins.Methods Four HLA-A02:01-restricted mRNA constructs were compared: single-9mer, multi-9mer, single-27mer, and multi-27mer, encoding the immunodominant influenza M1 epitope GILGFVFTL alongside eight subdominant filler epitopes in the multi-epitope conditions. Epitope-specific CD8 + T cell responses were quantified by MHC-I tetramer staining following in vitro priming with mRNA-electroporated autologous dendritic cells, with orthogonal readouts from 24-hour K562/Jurkat NFAT-luciferase TCR reporter assays and IFNγ ELISpot. A 16-epitope HPV16 9-mer polyepitope mRNA encoding validated multi HLA-restricted CTL epitopes from E2, E5, E6, and E7, HLA binding, and published human CTL reactivity was evaluated for multi-specific priming in HLA-A02:01+ primary human PBMCs by MHC-I tetramer staining, Jurkat NFAT-luciferase TCR reporter activation, and IFNγ ELISpot.Results Single-epitope encoding in 27-mer format modestly enhanced GILGFVFTL-tetramer + frequency over 9-mer (6.29% versus 4.72%). In the multi-epitope context, the 9-mer format imposed a ~50% reduction relative to the 27-mer ceiling (6.37% versus 3.36%), with the single-epitope 9-mer intermediate (4.72%), confirming inter-epitope competition as the dominant suppressive mechanism in compact constructs. TCR reporter activation mirrored this hierarchy: multi-27mer drove ~50-fold above-control activation versus ~25-fold for multi-9mer (p < 0.001). Despite the competition penalty inherent to the compact format, the 16-epitope universal PapillomaVax mRNA drove detectable and simultaneous CD8+ T cell responses against both E6 and E7 specificities in primary HLA-A*02:01+ PBMCs: E6-tetramer+ 9.49% and E7-tetramer+ 7.96% following PapillomaVax mRNA priming versus 0.42% and 0.11% in unstimulated controls, compared to 6.34% and 5.35% with cognate peptide stimulation. IFNγ ELISpot confirmed antigen-specific responses for PapillomaVax mRNA versus ~25 SFCs/5×105 for unstimulated controls (p < 0.001), exceeding both E7 peptide (~500 SFCs/5×105, p < 0.01) and E6 peptide (~550 SFCs/5×105, p < 0.001) restimulation conditions. Jurkat NFAT-luciferase TCR reporter activation confirmed MHC-I-restricted antigen presentation of both E6 (TIHDIILECV; 39-fold above control, p < 0.001) and E7 (YMLDLQPET; 24-fold above control, p < 0.001) specificities.Conclusions The 9-mer polyepitope format enables simultaneous multi-protein CTL priming across HPV16 E2, E5, E6, and E7 at a quantified and acceptable per-epitope cost.Ethics Approval IRB approved and available on request.

source_records.title: 1064 PapillomaVax: a compact 9-mer universal polyepitope mRNA vaccine spanning HPV16 E2, E5, E6, and E7 drives simultaneous multi-specific CD8 + T cell priming in primary human PBMCs
source_records.abstract: Background Therapeutic HPV vaccination requires broad, multi-specific CD8 + CTL responses against constitutively expressed viral oncoproteins to sustain tumor control and limit immune escape through selective antigen downregulation, documented in immune-edited HPV-positive tumors. Epitope-specific CD8 + T cell responses were quantified by MHC-I tetramer staining following in vitro priming with mRNA-electroporated autologous dendritic cells, with orthogonal readouts from 24-hour K562/Jurkat NFAT-luciferase TCR reporter assays and IFNγ ELISpot. Despite the competition penalty inherent to the compact format, the 16-epitope universal PapillomaVax mRNA drove detectable and simultaneous CD8+ T cell responses against both E6 and E7 specificities in primary HLA-A*02:01+ PBMCs: E6-tetramer+ 9.49% and E7-tetramer+ 7.96% following PapillomaVax mRNA priming versus 0.42% and 0.11% in unstimulated controls, compared to 6.34% and 5.35% with cognate peptide stimulation. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估 HPV16 特异性多表位 mRNA 疫苗 的紧凑 9 聚体格式的免疫成本及其在原代人 PBMC 中驱动同时多特异性 CD8 + T 细胞启动的能力。这一背景强调了针对 HPV 癌蛋白的广泛、多特异性 CD8 + CTL 反应的需要,以控制 HPV 阳性肿瘤。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究比较了四种 HLA-A02:01 限制性 mRNA 构建体:单 9mer、多 9mer、单 27mer 和多 27mer,编码免疫显性流感 M1 表位以及多表位条件下的 8 个次显性填充表位。该研究是在来自 HLA-A02:01+ 供体的原代人类 PBMC 中进行的。
elements_zh.methods: 表位特异性 CD8 + T 细胞反应通过 MHC-I 四聚体染色进行定量,然后用 mRNA 电穿孔的自体树突状细胞进行体外引发,并使用 24 小时 K562/Jurkat NFAT-荧光素酶 TCR 报告基因测定和 IFNγ ELISpot 的正交读数。
elements_zh.main_results: 相对于单表位 9 聚体中间体的 27 聚体上限,9 聚体形式使 CD8 + T 细胞反应降低约 50%。尽管存在竞争惩罚,但 16 个表位通用 PapillomaVax mRNA 在原代 HLA-A*02:01+ PBMC 中驱动了针对 E6 和 E7 特异性的可检测且同步的 CD8+ T 细胞反应。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究得出的结论是,9 聚体多表位格式能够以量化且可接受的每个表位成本同时启动跨 HPV16 E2、E5、E6 和 E7 的多蛋白 CTL。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,9 聚体格式可用于开发紧凑的 HPV16 特异性多表位 mRNA 疫苗,它可以驱动同时多特异性 CD8 + T 细胞启动,这对于治疗 HPV 疫苗接种 和肿瘤控制可能具有重要意义。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究设计的局限性包括使用单一 HLA-A02:01 限制性构建体以及需要在更大、更多样化的人群中进行进一步验证。由于证据仅具有抽象性质,证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 治疗性 HPV 疫苗接种 需要针对组成型表达的病毒癌蛋白的广泛、多特异性 CD8 + CTL 反应,以维持肿瘤控制并通过选择性抗原下调来限制免疫逃逸,这在免疫编辑的 HPV 阳性肿瘤中已有记录。27 聚体侧翼序列格式很常用,但其编码负担限制了多蛋白覆盖。我们系统地量化了紧凑 9 聚体格式的免疫成本,并将所得设计原理应用于编码来自 E2、E5、E6 和 E7 蛋白的已知免疫原性表位的 16 表位 HPV16 特异性多表位 mRNA。方法比较了四种 HLA-A02:01 限制性 mRNA 构建体:单 9 聚体、多 9 聚体、单 27 聚体和多 27 聚体,编码在多表位条件下,免疫显性流感 M1 表位 GILGFVFTL 与八个次显性填充表位一起。表位特异性 CD8 + T 细胞反应通过 MHC-I 四聚体染色进行定量,然后用 mRNA 电穿孔的自体树突状细胞进行体外引发,并使用 24 小时 K562/Jurkat NFAT-荧光素酶 TCR 报告基因测定和 IFNγ ELISpot 的正交读数。16 表位 HPV16 9 聚体多表位 mRNA 编码验证了来自 E2、E5、E6 和 E7 的多个 HLA 限制性 CTL 表位、HLA 结合和已发表的人 CTL 反应性,通过 MHC-I 四聚体染色、Jurkat NFAT-荧光素酶 TCR 报告基因激活和 IFNγ 评估 HLA-A02:01+ 原代人 PBMC 中的多特异性引发ELISpot.结果 与 9 聚体相比,27 聚体格式的单表位编码适度增强了 GILGFVFTL-四聚体 + 频率(6.29% 对比 4.72%)。在多表位背景下,9聚体形式相对于27聚体上限减少了约50%(6.37%对3.36%),单表位9聚体中间体(4.72%),证实表位间竞争是紧凑构建体中的主要抑制机制。TCR 报告基因激活反映了这种层次结构:多 27mer 驱动的激活比对照高约 50 倍,而多 9mer 则高出约 25 倍(p < 0.001)。尽管紧凑格式固有的竞争惩罚,16表位通用 PapillomaVax mRNA 在原代 HLA-A*02:01+ PBMC 中驱动可检测到的同时针对 E6 和 E7 特异性的 CD8+ T 细胞反应:PapillomaVax mRNA 引发后 E6-四聚体+ 9.49% 和 E7-四聚体+ 7.96%,而 PapillomaVax mRNA 引发后为 0.42% 和未刺激对照为 0.11%,而同源肽刺激为 6.34% 和 5.35%。IFNγ ELISpot 证实了 PapillomaVax mRNA 的抗原特异性反应,与未刺激对照的~25 SFCs/5×105 相比(p < 0.001),超过了 E7 肽(~500 SFCs/5×105,p < 0.01)和 E6 肽(~550 SFCs/5×105,p < 0.001)再刺激条件。Jurkat NFAT-荧光素酶 TCR 报告基因激活证实了 E6(TIHDIILECV;比对照高 39 倍,p < 0.001)和 E7(YMLDLQPET;比对照高 24 倍,p < 0.001)特异性的 MHC-I 限制性抗原呈递。结论 9 聚体多表位格式能够同时启动跨 HPV16 E2、E5、 E6 和 E7 以量化且可接受的每个表位成本。伦理审批 IRB 批准并可根据要求提供。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估 HPV16 特异性多表位 mRNA 疫苗 的紧凑 9 聚体格式的免疫成本及其在原代人 PBMC 中驱动同时多特异性 CD8 + T 细胞启动的能力。这一背景强调了针对 HPV 癌蛋白的广泛、多特异性 CD8 + CTL 反应的需要,以控制 HPV 阳性肿瘤。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究比较了四种 HLA-A02:01 限制性 mRNA 构建体:单 9mer、多 9mer、单 27mer 和多 27mer,编码免疫显性流感 M1 表位以及多表位条件下的 8 个次显性填充表位。该研究是在来自 HLA-A02:01+ 供体的原代人类 PBMC 中进行的。
analysis_zh.methods: 表位特异性 CD8 + T 细胞反应通过 MHC-I 四聚体染色进行定量,然后用 mRNA 电穿孔的自体树突状细胞进行体外引发,并使用 24 小时 K562/Jurkat NFAT-荧光素酶 TCR 报告基因测定和 IFNγ ELISpot 的正交读数。
analysis_zh.main_results: 相对于单表位 9 聚体中间体的 27 聚体上限,9 聚体形式使 CD8 + T 细胞反应降低约 50%。尽管存在竞争惩罚,但 16 个表位通用 PapillomaVax mRNA 在原代 HLA-A*02:01+ PBMC 中驱动了针对 E6 和 E7 特异性的可检测且同步的 CD8+ T 细胞反应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究得出的结论是,9 聚体多表位格式能够以量化且可接受的每个表位成本同时启动跨 HPV16 E2、E5、E6 和 E7 的多蛋白 CTL。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,9 聚体格式可用于开发紧凑的 HPV16 特异性多表位 mRNA 疫苗,它可以驱动同时多特异性 CD8 + T 细胞启动,这对于治疗 HPV 疫苗接种 和肿瘤控制可能具有重要意义。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究设计的局限性包括使用单一 HLA-A02:01 限制性构建体以及需要在更大、更多样化的人群中进行进一步验证。由于证据仅具有抽象性质,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Trends in Routine First-Dose Human Papillomavirus Vaccination Coverage in Wakayama Prefecture, Japan, Fiscal Years 2020–2025
papers.abstract: Abstract Background In Japan, proactive recommendations for human papillomavirus vaccination were suspended in 2013 and resumed in fiscal year 2022 alongside a catch-up program, whose first-dose eligibility ended in fiscal year 2024. Coverage among subsequent routine-vaccination cohorts remains unclear. We described first-dose vaccination coverage in Wakayama Prefecture during fiscal years 2020–2025, focusing on grade-specific differences between 2024 and 2025. Methods This descriptive epidemiological study used aggregated administrative data. Age-specific first-dose counts were obtained from e-Stat for fiscal years 2020–2021 and the Wakayama Prefectural Government for 2022–2025. Denominators were age-specific female populations from the 2020 Population Census. Vaccination counts and population data were reconstructed by birth fiscal year using a published method. Annual and cumulative coverage were estimated for the 2004–2013 birth cohorts. Results Between fiscal years 2024 and 2025, annual coverage changed from 3.8% to 4.1% in sixth-grade elementary school students, 20.6% to 15.4% in first-year junior high school students, 2.2% to 7.7% in second-year junior high school students, 30.5% to 16.4% in third-year junior high school students, and 13.1% to 6.1% in first-year high school students. Cumulative coverage by the end of first-year high school was 46.5% and 49.9% for the 2008 and 2009 birth cohorts, respectively. The highest-coverage grade shifted from first-year high school to third-year junior high school. Conclusions The predominant timing of first-dose vaccination shifted toward younger grades during fiscal years 2020–2025. However, annual coverage in 2025 was lower than in 2024 among first- and third-year junior high school students and first-year high school students.

analysis.main_results: Between fiscal years 2024 and 2025, annual coverage changed from 3.8% to 4.1% in sixth-grade elementary school students, 20.6% to 15.4% in first-year junior high school students, 2.2% to 7.7% in second-year junior high school students, 30.5% to 16.4% in third-year junior high school students, and 13.1% to 6.1% in first-year high school students. analysis.summary_en: This study examines trends in first-dose human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination coverage in Wakayama Prefecture, Japan, from fiscal years 2020 to 2025. It highlights shifts in vaccination timing among different grade levels, with the highest coverage moving to third-year junior high school students. The findings suggest a decline in annual coverage in 2025 compared to 2024 for several cohorts. The study uses aggregated administrative data and population census information to estimate coverage rates, providing insights into the effectiveness of vaccination programs in different age groups. However, the reliance on descriptive methods without deeper analysis limits the strength of the evidence, indicating a moderate confidence level in the conclusions.

papers.title_zh: 2020-2025 财年日本和歌山县常规首剂 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 覆盖率趋势
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background In Japan, proactive recommendations for human papillomavirus vaccination were suspended in 2013 and resumed in fiscal year 2022 alongside a catch-up program, whose first-dose eligibility ended in fiscal year 2024. Coverage among subsequent routine-vaccination cohorts remains unclear. We described first-dose vaccination coverage in Wakayama Prefecture during fiscal years 2020–2025, focusing on grade-specific differences between 2024 and 2025. Methods This descriptive epidemiological study used aggregated administrative data. Age-specific first-dose counts were obtained from e-Stat for fiscal years 2020–2021 and the Wakayama Prefectural Government for 2022–2025. Denominators were age-specific female populations from the 2020 Population Census. Vaccination counts and population data were reconstructed by birth fiscal year using a published method. Annual and cumulative coverage were estimated for the 2004–2013 birth cohorts. Results Between fiscal years 2024 and 2025, annual coverage changed from 3.8% to 4.1% in sixth-grade elementary school students, 20.6% to 15.4% in first-year junior high school students, 2.2% to 7.7% in second-year junior high school students, 30.5% to 16.4% in third-year junior high school students, and 13.1% to 6.1% in first-year high school students. Cumulative coverage by the end of first-year high school was 46.5% and 49.9% for the 2008 and 2009 birth cohorts, respectively. The highest-coverage grade shifted from first-year high school to third-year junior high school. Conclusions The predominant timing of first-dose vaccination shifted toward younger grades during fiscal years 2020–2025. However, annual coverage in 2025 was lower than in 2024 among first- and third-year junior high school students and first-year high school students.

papers.title: HUMAN PAPILLOMAVIRUS TYPE 16 AND 18 INFECTION ASSOCIATION WITH IL-38 GENE EXPRESSION IN IRAQI WOMEN WITH BREAST CANCER
papers.abstract: Introduction: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is implicated in the pathogenesis of several malignancies, and its possible role in breast cancer remains under investigation. This study aimed to explore the relationship between HPV infection and breast cancer and to assess its effect on the expression of interleukin-38 (IL-38). Methodology: The study population consisted of 40 patients and 39 control participants. HPV detection was performed by ELISA technique, followed by PCR for confirmation, while gene expression analysis of IL-38 was carried out in a subset of seven patients using housekeeping gene normalization. Results: ELISA results showed no positive cases among patients, whereas five control samples were positive. In contrast, PCR analysis was performed on 10 patients and 3 controls, the results showed that 8 of the patient samples were positive for both HPV types 18 and 16, while the controls had one positive for only HPV-16 and another sample was positive for both HPV-16 and -18. Gene expression analysis revealed altered expression of IL-38 among patients compared with controls, with most samples showing increased fold change. Discussion: Overall, the results are consistent with the hypothesis of possible prior exposure or latent HPV infection and suggest that treatment-related immune suppression may warrant further investigation. Dysregulation of IL-38 expression may suggest an immune response in HPV-associated breast cancer. Further investigation into a larger sample size is necessary to fully understand the molecular relationship between HPV infection, cytokine regulation and breast cancer progression.

papers.source_body_en: Introduction: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is implicated in the pathogenesis of several malignancies, and its possible role in breast cancer remains under investigation. This study aimed to explore the relationship between HPV infection and breast cancer and to assess its effect on the expression of interleukin-38 (IL-38). Methodology: The study population consisted of 40 patients and 39 control participants. HPV detection was performed by ELISA technique, followed by PCR for confirmation, while gene expression analysis of IL-38 was carried out in a subset of seven patients using housekeeping gene normalization. Results: ELISA results showed no positive cases among patients, whereas five control samples were positive. In contrast, PCR analysis was performed on 10 patients and 3 controls, the results showed that 8 of the patient samples were positive for both HPV types 18 and 16, while the controls had one positive for only HPV-16 and another sample was positive for both HPV-16 and -18. Gene expression analysis revealed altered expression of IL-38 among patients compared with controls, with most samples showing increased fold change. Discussion: Overall, the results are consistent with the hypothesis of possible prior exposure or latent HPV infection and suggest that treatment-related immune suppression may warrant further investigation. Dysregulation of IL-38 expression may suggest an immune response in HPV-associated breast cancer. Further investigation into a larger sample size is necessary to fully understand the molecular relationship between HPV infection, cytokine regulation and breast cancer progression.

papers.title: Sex disparities and catch-up opportunities in self-reported human papillomavirus vaccination at a Midwestern University in the United States
papers.abstract: Objective To assess sex disparities in self-reported human papillomavirus vaccination initiation and campus catch-up opportunities among undergraduates. Methods We analyzed baseline survey data collected February 23–March 13, 2023, from undergraduates aged 18–26 years at a public Midwestern university in the United States. The primary analysis included 115 students with known vaccination status; 50 with uncertain status were excluded. Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted prevalence ratios. Sensitivity analyses assigned uncertain responses as unvaccinated or vaccinated. Results Among students with known status, 68 of 115 (59.1%) reported initiation. Male students had lower adjusted initiation prevalence than female students (adjusted prevalence ratio, 0.50; 95% confidence interval, 0.31–0.79). Estimates remained below 1.00 when all uncertain responses were assigned as unvaccinated (0.36; 0.21–0.61) or vaccinated (0.80; 0.64–0.99). Of 47 students reporting no vaccination, 57.4% expressed hypothetical willingness following healthcare professional advice and 48.9% if vaccination were offered on campus; corresponding proportions among 50 students with uncertain status were 62.0% and 52.0%. Conclusions Self-reported initiation was lower among male undergraduates across sensitivity scenarios. Record verification and prospective evaluation of recommendation and campus delivery are warranted.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究分析了2023年2月23日至3月13日从美国中西部一所公立大学收集的18-26岁本科生的基线调查数据。主要分析包括115名已知疫苗接种状态的学生,排除了50名状态不确定的学生。
elements_zh.methods: 使用改进的泊松回归来估计调整后的 患病率 比率,并通过将不确定的响应分配为未接种疫苗或接种疫苗来进行敏感性分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 在已知状况的学生中,115 名学生中的 68 名 (59.1%) 报告了启蒙。男学生的调整起始 患病率 低于女学生(调整后 患病率 比率,0.50;95% 置信区间,0.31–0.79)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,在不同敏感情况下,男性本科生自我报告的感染起始率较低,这突显了有关 HPV 疫苗接种 性别差异的新发现。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明需要采取有针对性的干预措施来解决 HPV 疫苗接种 中的性别差异,并为基于校园的追赶计划提供了机会。

papers.title_zh: 美国中西部大学自我报告人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种中的性别差异和追赶机会
papers.source_body_en: Objective To assess sex disparities in self-reported human papillomavirus vaccination initiation and campus catch-up opportunities among undergraduates. Methods We analyzed baseline survey data collected February 23–March 13, 2023, from undergraduates aged 18–26 years at a public Midwestern university in the United States. The primary analysis included 115 students with known vaccination status; 50 with uncertain status were excluded. Modified Poisson regression estimated adjusted prevalence ratios. Sensitivity analyses assigned uncertain responses as unvaccinated or vaccinated. Results Among students with known status, 68 of 115 (59.1%) reported initiation. Male students had lower adjusted initiation prevalence than female students (adjusted prevalence ratio, 0.50; 95% confidence interval, 0.31–0.79). Estimates remained below 1.00 when all uncertain responses were assigned as unvaccinated (0.36; 0.21–0.61) or vaccinated (0.80; 0.64–0.99). Of 47 students reporting no vaccination, 57.4% expressed hypothetical willingness following healthcare professional advice and 48.9% if vaccination were offered on campus; corresponding proportions among 50 students with uncertain status were 62.0% and 52.0%. Conclusions Self-reported initiation was lower among male undergraduates across sensitivity scenarios. Record verification and prospective evaluation of recommendation and campus delivery are warranted.
papers.abstract_zh: 目的 评估本科生自我报告的 人乳头瘤病毒 疫苗接种 启动和校园追赶机会的性别差异。方法 我们分析了 2023 年 2 月 23 日至 3 月 13 日从美国中西部一所公立大学 18 至 26 岁本科生收集的基线调查数据。主要分析包括 115 名已知 疫苗接种 状态的学生;排除了 50 名身份不明的人。修正泊松回归估计调整后的 患病率 比率。敏感性分析将不确定的反应指定为未接种疫苗或接种疫苗。结果 在已知状况的学生中,115 名学生中有 68 名 (59.1%) 报告开始学习。男学生的调整起始 患病率 低于女学生(调整后 患病率 比率,0.50;95% 置信区间,0.31–0.79)。当所有不确定的反应被指定为未接种疫苗(0.36;0.21-0.61)或接种疫苗(0.80;0.64-0.99)时,估计值仍低于 1.00。在 47 名报告没有 疫苗接种 的学生中,57.4% 的学生表示假设愿意遵循医疗保健专业建议,而 48.9% 的学生表示愿意在校园内提供 疫苗接种;50名学生中,身份不明的相应比例分别为62.0%和52.0%。结论 在各种敏感性情景中,男大学生自我报告的开始程度较低。推荐和校园交付的记录验证和前瞻性评估是有必要的。

papers.title: Association of classical sexually transmitted infections and genital mycoplasmas detection with high-risk human papillomavirus and cervical lesions among women undergoing cervical cancer screening in Ethiopia
papers.abstract: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infection is the necessary cause of cervical cancer. A small proportion of HPV infections may progress to high-grade cervical lesions or cancer. Genital mycoplasma and sexually transmitted infections (STIs) may be associated with HPV persistence and progression. These detections or infections may also reduce the diagnostic accuracy of visual inspection-based screening by increasing local inflammation. In Ethiopia, there is still limited evidence on the association of STIs and genital mycoplasmas with hrHPV, cervical lesions, and visual inspection with acetic acid or Lugol’s iodine (VILI/VILI). This study assessed the prevalence of certain classical STIs and genital mycoplasma, their association with hrHPV infection, cervical lesions, and VIA/VILI outcomes among women undergoing HPV-based cervical cancer screening. Vaginal self-samples from 885 Ethiopian women were tested for 14 hrHPV types, C. trachomatis (CT), N. gonorrhoeae (NG), T. vaginalis (TV), and four genital mycoplasmas using real-time PCR. One hundred and fifty-six women who tested positive for hrHPV underwent VIA/VILI, and 116 women underwent histology examinations. Frequencies and percentages were used to summarize descriptive statistics of categorical variables. The prevalence estimates were provided with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), using the Wilson score method. Associations were assessed by the chi-square test and logistic regression analysis between the independent and outcome variables. A Firth-penalized multivariable logistic regression analysis was also used for histological results and independent variables. Among the study participants, 568 women (64.2%) had at least one sexually transmitted microbe (STM) (95% CI: 61–67). Classical STIs were detected in 4.3% (95% CI: 3.1–5.8), and genital mycoplasmas in 64% (95% CI: 60.7–67.1) of participants. parvum was the most frequently detected species. High-risk HPV infection was associated with genital mycoplasma detection (AOR = 1.7, 95% CI: 1.3–2.3, p = 0.001), C. trachomatis infection (AOR = 5.4, 95% CI: 1.4–21, p = 0.014), M. hominis detection (AOR = 2.0, 95% CI: 1.4-3.0, p = 0.001), and HIV infection (AOR = 3.2, 95% CI: 1.8–5.5, p < 0.001). CIN2 + lesions were associated with both hrHPV (AOR = 6.77, 95% CI: 1.2–75.4, P = 0.03) and HIV infection (AOR = 8.92, 95% CI: 1.5–72.2, P = 0.02). Neither STIs nor genital mycoplasma detection were associated with VIA/VILI outcomes. Classical STIs were low among the women included in the study. However, one out of five women were infected with hrHPV, and 64% of the women were harbored genital mycoplasma. HrHPV infection was associated with genital mycoplasma detection, C. trachomatis infection , M. hominis detection, and HIV infection. HrHPV and HIV infections were associated with CIN2 + lesions, whereas classical STIs and genital mycoplasma were not associated with cervical abnormalities. There was no association between STIs or the detection of genital mycoplasma and the outcomes of VIA/VILI. Overall, this study emphasizes the importance of considering HPV–HIV co-infections in cervical cancer prevention strategies.

analysis.methods: Vaginal self-samples were tested for 14 hrHPV types and classical STIs using real-time PCR, and associations were assessed with chi-square tests and logistic regression analyses, including Firth-penalized multivariable logistic regression for histological results.

papers.title_zh: 在埃塞俄比亚接受 宫颈癌 筛查的女性中,经典性传播感染和生殖器支原体检测与高风险 人乳头瘤病毒 和宫颈病变的关联
papers.source_body_en: Persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) infection is the necessary cause of cervical cancer. A small proportion of HPV infections may progress to high-grade cervical lesions or cancer. Genital mycoplasma and sexually transmitted infections (STIs) may be associated with HPV persistence and progression. These detections or infections may also reduce the diagnostic accuracy of visual inspection-based screening by increasing local inflammation. In Ethiopia, there is still limited evidence on the association of STIs and genital mycoplasmas with hrHPV, cervical lesions, and visual inspection with acetic acid or Lugol’s iodine (VILI/VILI). This study assessed the prevalence of certain classical STIs and genital mycoplasma, their association with hrHPV infection, cervical lesions, and VIA/VILI outcomes among women undergoing HPV-based cervical cancer screening. Vaginal self-samples from 885 Ethiopian women were tested for 14 hrHPV types, C. trachomatis (CT), N. gonorrhoeae (NG), T. vaginalis (TV), and four genital mycoplasmas using real-time PCR. One hundred and fifty-six women who tested positive for hrHPV underwent VIA/VILI, and 116 women underwent histology examinations. Frequencies and percentages were used to summarize descriptive statistics of categorical variables. The prevalence estimates were provided with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), using the Wilson score method. Associations were assessed by the chi-square test and logistic regression analysis between the independent and outcome variables. A Firth-penalized multivariable logistic regression analysis was also used for histological results and independent variables. Among the study participants, 568 women (64.2%) had at least one sexually transmitted microbe (STM) (95% CI: 61–67). Classical STIs were detected in 4.3% (95% CI: 3.1–5.8), and genital mycoplasmas in 64% (95% CI: 60.7–67.1) of participants. parvum was the most frequently detected species. High-risk HPV infection was associated with genital mycoplasma detection (AOR = 1.7, 95% CI: 1.3–2.3, p = 0.001), C. trachomatis infection (AOR = 5.4, 95% CI: 1.4–21, p = 0.014), M. hominis detection (AOR = 2.0, 95% CI: 1.4-3.0, p = 0.001), and HIV infection (AOR = 3.2, 95% CI: 1.8–5.5, p < 0.001). CIN2 + lesions were associated with both hrHPV (AOR = 6.77, 95% CI: 1.2–75.4, P = 0.03) and HIV infection (AOR = 8.92, 95% CI: 1.5–72.2, P = 0.02). Neither STIs nor genital mycoplasma detection were associated with VIA/VILI outcomes. Classical STIs were low among the women included in the study. However, one out of five women were infected with hrHPV, and 64% of the women were harbored genital mycoplasma. HrHPV infection was associated with genital mycoplasma detection, C. trachomatis infection , M. hominis detection, and HIV infection. HrHPV and HIV infections were associated with CIN2 + lesions, whereas classical STIs and genital mycoplasma were not associated with cervical abnormalities. There was no association between STIs or the detection of genital mycoplasma and the outcomes of VIA/VILI. Overall, this study emphasizes the importance of considering HPV–HIV co-infections in cervical cancer prevention strategies.

papers.title: 852 ABS005, a novel hydrogel, for treatment of high-grade cervical intraepithelial neoplasia
papers.abstract: Background Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN 2/3) management relies on excisional or ablative procedures. 1 While effective, these interventions are associated with cervical stenosis,2 increased rates of preterm birth and miscarriage,3–5 and do not address the underlying human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, leading to persistence and recurrence. Absco Therapeutics has developed ABS005, a treatment for CIN2/3. ABS005 incorporates imiquimod, a TLR7 agonist used off-label for CIN2/3 with modest efficacy against both the lesion and HPV.6 However, topical formulations are limited by poor retention and washout.7 ABS005 is intended for direct intracervical injection, forming a depot for sustained, on-target imiquimod delivery. ABS005 is designed to eliminate CIN2/3 lesions and educate the immune system against HPV infection. This approach may preserve cervical integrity and future obstetric outcomes, providing women non-surgical treatment options.Methods The hydrogel properties and in vitro release profile of ABS005 were first characterized. To evaluate in vivo efficacy, single and multiple ABS005 treatments were assessed in a murine model of cervical cancer where HPV-positive Tal3 tumor cells are inoculated into C57BL/6 mouse flanks.8 9 Flow cytometry characterized the intratumoral response, profiling antigen presenting cells (CD80+ and 86+), dendritic cells (CD11c+), anti-tumor macrophage (F4/80+), cytotoxic T-cell (CD4+/CD8+) and NK-cell populations (CD45+/CD3-/CD49b+). Local-to-systemic therapeutic ratios were defined by comparing intratumoral and systemic drug pharmacokinetic profiles. Finally, we characterized the toxicokinetic profile of ABS005 following intracervical injection in canines.Results We formulated a polymer that solidifies into a gel at 34°C (±2°C) and provides sustained drug release over 48 hours in vitro and at least one week in vivo. In the murine model, both single and multiple treatments of ABS005 successfully halted tumor growth (figure 1) and stimulated an intratumoral immune profile consistent with imiquimod’s mechanism of action. Pharmacokinetic analysis revealed exceptional local retention, with intratumoral imiquimod concentrations exceeding systemic levels by 20,000-fold (figure 2). Furthermore, canine intracervical injections demonstrated that ABS005 was well tolerated, with a peak plasma Cmax of 19.4 ng/mL at 30 minutes post-treatment.Conclusions These data suggest that ABS005 can provide a sustained, controlled release of imiquimod to treat HPV-driven dysplasia while maintaining a favorable safety profile. Next steps include GMP-grade manufacturing, GLP toxicology, and FDA clearance of an investigational new drug application.Acknowledgements We appreciate Prof. Giovanni Traverso (MIT, Absco Therapeutics) and Prof. Avik Som (U Washington, Absco Therapeutics) for scientific discussions. papers.abstract_original: Background Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN 2/3) management relies on excisional or ablative procedures. 1 While effective, these interventions are associated with cervical stenosis,2 increased rates of preterm birth and miscarriage,3–5 and do not address the underlying human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, leading to persistence and recurrence. Absco Therapeutics has developed ABS005, a treatment for CIN2/3. ABS005 incorporates imiquimod, a TLR7 agonist used off-label for CIN2/3 with modest efficacy against both the lesion and HPV.6 However, topical formulations are limited by poor retention and washout.7 ABS005 is intended for direct intracervical injection, forming a depot for sustained, on-target imiquimod delivery. ABS005 is designed to eliminate CIN2/3 lesions and educate the immune system against HPV infection. This approach may preserve cervical integrity and future obstetric outcomes, providing women non-surgical treatment options.Methods The hydrogel properties and in vitro release profile of ABS005 were first characterized. To evaluate in vivo efficacy, single and multiple ABS005 treatments were assessed in a murine model of cervical cancer where HPV-positive Tal3 tumor cells are inoculated into C57BL/6 mouse flanks.8 9 Flow cytometry characterized the intratumoral response, profiling antigen presenting cells (CD80+ and 86+), dendritic cells (CD11c+), anti-tumor macrophage (F4/80+), cytotoxic T-cell (CD4+/CD8+) and NK-cell populations (CD45+/CD3-/CD49b+). Local-to-systemic therapeutic ratios were defined by comparing intratumoral and systemic drug pharmacokinetic profiles. Finally, we characterized the toxicokinetic profile of ABS005 following intracervical injection in canines.Results We formulated a polymer that solidifies into a gel at 34°C (±2°C) and provides sustained drug release over 48 hours in vitro and at least one week in vivo. In the murine model, both single and multiple treatments of ABS005 successfully halted tumor growth (figure 1) and stimulated an intratumoral immune profile consistent with imiquimod’s mechanism of action. Pharmacokinetic analysis revealed exceptional local retention, with intratumoral imiquimod concentrations exceeding systemic levels by 20,000-fold (figure 2). Furthermore, canine intracervical injections demonstrated that ABS005 was well tolerated, with a peak plasma Cmax of 19.4 ng/mL at 30 minutes post-treatment.Conclusions These data suggest that ABS005 can provide a sustained, controlled release of imiquimod to treat HPV-driven dysplasia while maintaining a favorable safety profile. analysis.summary_en: This study presents ABS005, a novel hydrogel designed for the treatment of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN 2/3) and HPV-driven dysplasia. The research highlights the limitations of current excisional or ablative procedures, which are associated with complications such as cervical stenosis, preterm birth, and miscarriage. ABS005 incorporates imiquimod, a TLR7 agonist, and is intended for direct intracervical injection to provide sustained drug release. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrated that ABS005 effectively halted tumor growth in a murine model and showed exceptional local retention of imiquimod, with concentrations exceeding systemic levels by 20,000-fold. Canine studies indicated that ABS005 was well tolerated. The authors interpret these findings as suggesting that ABS005 could offer a non-surgical treatment option for HPV-related cervical lesions, preserving cervical integrity and obstetric outcomes. The study's significance lies in its potential to inform future research on localized drug delivery for HPV-associated diseases. However, the evidence is limited to animal models, and the study does not include human clinical trials, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 宫颈上皮内瘤变 (CIN 2/3) 的治疗依赖于切除或消融手术,这些手术与宫颈狭窄、早产和流产率增加等并发症相关,并且不能解决潜在的 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染,从而导致持续存在和复发。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究评估了 ABS005 在 宫颈癌 小鼠模型中的体内功效,其中 HPV 阳性 Tal3 肿瘤细胞被接种到 C57BL/6 小鼠胁腹中。它还表征了犬科动物宫颈内注射后 ABS005 的毒代动力学特征。
elements_zh.methods: 首先对 ABS005 的水凝胶特性和体外释放曲线进行了表征。为了评估体内功效,在 宫颈癌 的小鼠模型中评估了单个和多个 ABS005 治疗,并进行药代动力学分析以比较瘤内和全身药物分布。
elements_zh.main_results: ABS005 经配制可在 34°C (±2°C) 下固化成凝胶,并在体外提供超过 48 小时的持续药物释放,在体内提供至少一周的持续药物释放。在小鼠模型中,ABS005 的单个和多个 治疗 均成功阻止了肿瘤生长,并刺激了与咪喹莫特作用机制一致的瘤内免疫特征。药代动力学分析显示,咪喹莫特具有出色的局部滞留性,瘤内浓度超过全身水平 20,000 倍。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些数据表明 ABS005 可以提供咪喹莫特的持续、受控释放,以治疗 HPV 驱动的发育不良,同时保持良好的安全性。这种方法可以保留宫颈完整性和未来的产科结果,为女性提供非手术 治疗 选择。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 它可以为未来关于 HPV 相关 宫颈癌 局部药物输送的研究提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于小鼠模型和犬毒代动力学分析,可能无法完全代表人类生理学。证据是中等的,因为这些发现是基于体外和动物研究,没有进行人体临床试验。

CIN2/3 标签外治疗的 TLR7 激动剂,对病变和 HPV 的疗效均有限。6 然而,局部制剂因保留性和冲洗性差而受到限制。7 ABS005 旨在用于直接宫颈内注射,形成持续、靶向咪喹莫特递送的储库。ABS005 旨在消除 CIN2/3 病变并教育免疫系统抵抗 HPV 感染。这种方法可以保留宫颈完整性和未来的产科结果,为女性提供非手术 治疗 选择。方法首先对 ABS005 的水凝胶特性和体外释放曲线进行了表征。为了评估体内功效,在 宫颈癌 小鼠模型中评估了单个和多个 ABS005 治疗,其中 HPV 阳性 Tal3 肿瘤细胞接种到 C57BL/6 小鼠胁腹中。8 9 流式细胞术表征肿瘤内反应,分析抗原呈递细胞(CD80+ 和 86+)、树突状细胞 (CD11c+)、抗肿瘤巨噬细胞(F4/80+)、细胞毒性 T 细胞 (CD4+/CD8+) 和 NK 细胞群 papers.title: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells and M2 macrophages are associated with clinical outcomes in human papillomavirus–independent vulvar squamous cell carcinoma
papers.abstract: Background Vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC) is a rare malignancy comprising HPV-associated (HPV-A) and HPV-independent (HPV-I) subtypes. HPV-I is associated with high recurrence rates and poor survival, yet lacks validated prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic stratification tools. Although immunotherapy has transformed cancer care and highlighted the tumor microenvironment (TME) as an important determinant of clinical outcome, the rarity of VSCC has limited its molecular characterization, and the TME remains poorly understood. We therefore aimed to define the VSCC TME in an HPV-specific context and identify immune features associated with clinical outcomes. Methods We analyzed 70 surgically treated VSCC (18 HPV-A and 52 HPV-I) using targeted transcriptomic profiling (HTG EdgeSeq). Immune and stromal cell composition was inferred by computational deconvolution, primarily with xCell and supported by EPIC, quanTIseq and MCPcounter. TME composition was compared by HPV status and, within HPV-I VSCC, by p53 and PD-L1 immunohistochemical status. Associations with recurrence-free and disease-specific survival were assessed using Firth-penalized Cox regression adjusted for FIGO stage and p53 status, and candidate populations were evaluated by CD123 and CD163 immunohistochemistry. Results HPV-A tumors showed higher immune and overall microenvironment scores, with enrichment of diverse lymphoid and myeloid populations, whereas HPV-I tumors showed lower immune-cell enrichment. Within HPV-I VSCC, plasmacytoid dendritic cell (pDC) enrichment showed the most consistent association with favorable survival across deconvolution-based analyses, with immunohistochemistry confirming CD123 + cell infiltration as an independent favorable prognostic factor. PD-L1 positivity occurred in 44% of HPV-I tumors and was associated with CD163 + macrophage infiltration, which, in turn, was independently associated with poor outcomes. Conclusions TME profiling identified two clinically relevant immune populations within HPV-I VSCC: CD123 + cell infiltration was associated with favorable outcomes, whereas CD163 + macrophage infiltration was associated with PD-L1 positivity and poorer outcomes. These findings provide a rationale for further investigation of the TME as a source of prognostic and potentially therapeutic biomarkers. Validation in larger, independent cohorts is required before clinical utility can be established.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the tumor microenvironment (TME) of vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC) in an HPV-specific context, focusing on HPV-independent subtypes. The research aimed to identify immune features linked to clinical outcomes. Using transcriptomic profiling and computational deconvolution, the study found that HPV-independent tumors had lower immune-cell enrichment compared to HPV-associated ones. The findings suggest that TME components could serve as prognostic and therapeutic biomarkers, though further validation in larger cohorts is needed. The study highlights the importance of understanding immune dynamics in HPV-independent VSCC for improved treatment strategies.

papers.title_zh: 浆细胞样树突状细胞和 M2 巨噬细胞与 人乳头瘤病毒 独立外阴鳞状细胞癌的临床结果相关
papers.source_body_en: Background Vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC) is a rare malignancy comprising HPV-associated (HPV-A) and HPV-independent (HPV-I) subtypes. HPV-I is associated with high recurrence rates and poor survival, yet lacks validated prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic stratification tools. Although immunotherapy has transformed cancer care and highlighted the tumor microenvironment (TME) as an important determinant of clinical outcome, the rarity of VSCC has limited its molecular characterization, and the TME remains poorly understood. We therefore aimed to define the VSCC TME in an HPV-specific context and identify immune features associated with clinical outcomes. Methods We analyzed 70 surgically treated VSCC (18 HPV-A and 52 HPV-I) using targeted transcriptomic profiling (HTG EdgeSeq). Immune and stromal cell composition was inferred by computational deconvolution, primarily with xCell and supported by EPIC, quanTIseq and MCPcounter. TME composition was compared by HPV status and, within HPV-I VSCC, by p53 and PD-L1 immunohistochemical status. Associations with recurrence-free and disease-specific survival were assessed using Firth-penalized Cox regression adjusted for FIGO stage and p53 status, and candidate populations were evaluated by CD123 and CD163 immunohistochemistry. Results HPV-A tumors showed higher immune and overall microenvironment scores, with enrichment of diverse lymphoid and myeloid populations, whereas HPV-I tumors showed lower immune-cell enrichment. Within HPV-I VSCC, plasmacytoid dendritic cell (pDC) enrichment showed the most consistent association with favorable survival across deconvolution-based analyses, with immunohistochemistry confirming CD123 + cell infiltration as an independent favorable prognostic factor. PD-L1 positivity occurred in 44% of HPV-I tumors and was associated with CD163 + macrophage infiltration, which, in turn, was independently associated with poor outcomes. Conclusions TME profiling identified two clinically relevant immune populations within HPV-I VSCC: CD123 + cell infiltration was associated with favorable outcomes, whereas CD163 + macrophage infiltration was associated with PD-L1 positivity and poorer outcomes. These findings provide a rationale for further investigation of the TME as a source of prognostic and potentially therapeutic biomarkers. Validation in larger, independent cohorts is required before clinical utility can be established.

papers.title: Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles delivering CERS1 promote squamous differentiation in HPV16-positive cervical intraepithelial neoplasia via remodeling sphingomyelin metabolism
papers.abstract: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), a precursor of human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven cervical cancer, poses a severe threat to women’s health. High-risk HPV infection drives CIN progression, whereas well-defined intervention targets and effective non-invasive therapies remain lacking. Herein, Using New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), specifically HPV16-positive ectocervical organoids as a human-relevant disease model, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of engineered cell-free small extracellular vesicles derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hucMSC-sEV). We found that hucMSC-sEV significantly promoted squamous differentiation in S12 cells and HPV16-positive ectocervical organoids. Mechanistically, integrated multi-omics analyses within this NAMs platform revealed that hucMSC-sEV delivered ceramide synthase 1 (CERS1) to upregulate C18 ceramide (C18 Cer) synthesis, activating the non-canonical p53 signaling to drive squamous differentiation. In NCG mice bearing subcutaneous xenografts of S12 cells, hucMSC-sEV effectively inhibited S12 xenograft growth and modulated squamous differentiation via regulation of C18 ceramide metabolism, while this therapeutic effect was abrogated in CERS1-knockdown hucMSC-sEV. This study delineates the molecular mechanism by which hucMSC-sEV remodel sphingolipid metabolism to promote cervical squamous epithelial differentiation and suppress S12 xenograft development, providing novel potential targets and therapeutic strategies for CIN intervention.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the therapeutic potential of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles (hucMSC-sEV) in HPV16-positive cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN). The research aims to address the lack of effective non-invasive therapies for CIN, a precursor to cervical cancer. Using HPV16-positive ectocervical organoids as a disease model, the study demonstrates that hucMSC-sEV significantly promote squamous differentiation in CIN cells. Mechanistically, the vesicles deliver ceramide synthase 1 (CERS1), upregulating C18 ceramide synthesis and activating non-canonical p53 signaling to drive differentiation. In vivo experiments in NCG mice show that hucMSC-sEV inhibit xenograft growth and modulate differentiation through C18 ceramide metabolism. The findings suggest a novel molecular mechanism and therapeutic strategy for CIN intervention. However, the study is limited to an in vitro and in vivo model, and the results may not fully translate to human clinical settings.

papers.title_zh: 人脐带间充质干细胞来源的小细胞外囊泡传递 CERS1 通过重塑鞘磷脂代谢促进 HPV16 阳性宫颈上皮内瘤变的鳞状细胞分化
papers.source_body_en: Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN), a precursor of human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven cervical cancer, poses a severe threat to women’s health. High-risk HPV infection drives CIN progression, whereas well-defined intervention targets and effective non-invasive therapies remain lacking. Herein, Using New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), specifically HPV16-positive ectocervical organoids as a human-relevant disease model, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of engineered cell-free small extracellular vesicles derived from human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hucMSC-sEV). We found that hucMSC-sEV significantly promoted squamous differentiation in S12 cells and HPV16-positive ectocervical organoids. Mechanistically, integrated multi-omics analyses within this NAMs platform revealed that hucMSC-sEV delivered ceramide synthase 1 (CERS1) to upregulate C18 ceramide (C18 Cer) synthesis, activating the non-canonical p53 signaling to drive squamous differentiation. In NCG mice bearing subcutaneous xenografts of S12 cells, hucMSC-sEV effectively inhibited S12 xenograft growth and modulated squamous differentiation via regulation of C18 ceramide metabolism, while this therapeutic effect was abrogated in CERS1-knockdown hucMSC-sEV. This study delineates the molecular mechanism by which hucMSC-sEV remodel sphingolipid metabolism to promote cervical squamous epithelial differentiation and suppress S12 xenograft development, providing novel potential targets and therapeutic strategies for CIN intervention.

papers.title: 621 Pelareorep and atezolizumab-induced expansion of HPV-16-specific T cells in the blood is associated with tumor responses in squamous cell anal cancer
papers.abstract: Background Squamous cell anal cancer (SCAC) is a rare disease representing approximately 2.6% of GI cancers. Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the main cause of SCAC. Treatment options for ≥2L SCAC are limited. Checkpoint inhibitors (CPI) are recommended for immunotherapy naïve patients who failed 1L chemotherapy, but response rates are low. The oncolytic reovirus pelareorep (pela) combined with atezolizumab (atezo) has shown promise as a ≥2L treatment in this population. In pancreatic cancer patients treated with pela and atezo, tumor responses are associated with tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL) and mRAS clonal expansion in the blood. Here, we report the association between SCAC tumor responses, TIL infiltration, and HPV-16-specific clonal expansion in the blood. We also report post-therapy changes in the levels of plasma analytes that are associated with responses to checkpoint inhibitor therapyMethods A phase 1/2, Simon 2-stage study is being conducted to assess the safety and efficacy of pela in combination with atezo as a ≥2L therapy in patients with unresectable SCAC ( NCT07280377). Patients were treated IV with pela 4.5 x 1010 TCID50 weekly and atezo 840 mg biweekly on a 28-day cycle. Pre-treatment tumors were available from 4 patients to identify TILs by T-cell receptor sequencing (Adaptive Biotechnologies, Seattle, WA), and blood from these patients was analyzed for the expansion of TIL clones from baseline through 3 cycles. Blood from 14 patients was analyzed for HPV-16-specific clonal expansion by the Multiplexed Identification of T-cell Antigen Specificity assay (MIRA assay, Adaptive Biotechnologies). Plasma analytes including CXCL10, IFN-γ, and sPD-L1 were measured by the Olink assay in 8 patients after one cycle of therapy.Results Increases (> 2-fold) in CXCL10, IFN-γ, and sPD-L1 were observed in 7/8 subjects. TIL clonal expansion in the blood was observed after 3 cycles in all 4 patients and was associated with reductions in tumor size (2 complete and 2 partial responses per RECIST). These patients also showed a significant increase in at least one HPV-16-specific clone. Of the 14 patients evaluated, 6 had HPV-16 clonal expansion, and 4 of these showed a reduction in tumor size.Conclusions Pela + atezo can achieve favorable tumor responses in ≥2 nd-line SCAC. These responses are associated with HPV-16-specific and TIL clonal expansion in the blood. The favorable changes in plasma analyte levels were also associated with the immune control of tumors. Together, these data support further evaluation of pela and CPI as an immunotherapy for SCAC.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between tumor responses in squamous cell anal cancer (SCAC) and the expansion of HPV-16-specific T cells in the blood following treatment with pelareorep and atezolizumab. The research highlights that tumor responses are linked to TIL infiltration and HPV-16-specific clonal expansion, suggesting a potential role for these immune markers in monitoring treatment efficacy. The findings support further exploration of this combination therapy as an immunotherapy option for ≥2L SCAC. However, the study is limited to an abstract-only analysis, and no detailed limitations or evidence strength are reported.
